title: What bands played when he started: songs and blues
summary: Early bands played songs like Japanese Sandman and blues such as How Come You Do Me Like You Do, St. Louis, Memphis and Beale Street Blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: But when you first started playing with bands, they weren't playing Dixieland or they weren't playing Ragtime.
What were they playing? Did you call it anything?
Let me think if I can think of any songs. I'm trying to think of something ...(?)...(? )...
That was one of the songs we used to play. That don't sound like Dixieland, does it?
No. Well, it's a song. So is it playing songs that makes the difference?
Playing songs! Yeah. At the time I got on, I was playing some ...(? )... blues, you know -- things like that.

Well, you say Blues... Would you be playing the Blues in the sense that you could say today, if you're calling a tune, "Let's play the Blues in B-flat"... Could you do that then? Or was it a Blues like a specific that was based on the Blues?
Well, some of them I would say was just plain Blues. Some of them was taking a song like "How Come You Do Me Like You Do?" Now, that's a sort of a Blues. You know?

It's got the stop time in it. [SINGS REFRAIN] I think that was around at the time I came along. Then they had the "Saint Louis Blues" and the "Memphis Blues" and the "Beale Street Blues." They were distinctly different Blues. "Tishomango Blues" was a different Blues than the others.
That's really almost like a song form.
Yes, that's a song. Yes, it is!
Now, you were just talking about that stop time thing in "How Come You Do Me Like You Do."
